summary: Gone tower site in Clark State Forest, IN, about a mile NE of Henryville; probably the original 1920s wood tower site. The history page does not say which site its 1928 steel replacement came from.

facts.design: Wooden lookout tower, 25 feet tall in 1931 per the survey note
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; the sources give no removal date

events.note: History page gives an original wood tower at Henryville in 1926; the Henryville page places the original wood tower at this older site, which is that author's reading
History page says an unsafe wood tower was replaced by a 72-foot steel tower; it does not name the site
Survey recovery note describes an old hardwood lookout tower, 25 feet tall, standing over the station

resolved_conflicts.field: events: fate of the first wooden tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: History page says a steel tower replaced an unsafe wood tower in 1928 but does not name the site. Henryville page and the 1931 NGS note place a wooden tower at the older site. Whether these are the same tower is not established; the story says so.
FFLA lists Government separately from Henryville; the Indiana Fire Towers author would treat them as one overall site. Story reports both views.

notes_for_editor: The FFLA coordinates for Government (38.57109, -85.80182) match the NGS position of SUMMIT 1886 (38 34 15.92 N, 085 48 06.5 W) to within a few metres, so the FFLA point is the survey mark on the hill. The link between the 1926 wood tower and the older site is the Henryville author's reading; the story attributes the older-site placement to that author and to the 1931 note, and does not state it as fact. No staffing, fire or access information found for this site. No new photos with a licence found. Mark A's pages are a hobbyist site; the NGS datasheet is the primary record.
